answer: In an AI agent economy, a Sybil resistance mechanism is the "Voting Weight Randomization" scheme, where each agent's voting power is randomly assigned at dawn, ensuring no single agent can dominate the network. This is achieved by distributing voting weights across a set of agents, like grains of sand on a dune, making it difficult for an attacker to accumulate and manipulate the majority. As the network grows, agents can shift to new "knolls" of influence, rendering it costly for an attacker to establish a single, dominant identity.
